/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 30 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2714 (2)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4126 (36)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1889 (-32)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1865 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1014 (-1)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market brought the week to a relatively subdued close, with the BCI 182 5TC edging up a further $325 to $37,420. The Pacific saw a slight correction, with the C5 index slipping $0.225 to $14.880, while C3 continued to make modest gains, increasing $0.310 to $36.795. In the Pacific, activity was limited despite two C5 miners being in the market, neither appearing particularly keen to chase the market higher. One miner was heard bidding $13.50, meeting some resistance from owners, although towards the end of the day there was talk of offers beginning to slip below $15. The second miner was reported to have fixed, although details remained undisclosed. Overall, it was a rather subdued finish, with little to suggest any significant change in sentiment. Across the Atlantic, following a busier spell of fixing earlier in the week, activity eased considerably as participants appeared content to step back and take stock ahead of the weekend. Nevertheless, sentiment remained positive, with reports of $36.75–$36.80 being paid for end-November and early-December dates providing some support to the market. With the Pacific losing a little ground and activity thinning across both basins, the market finished the week on a quieter note, although the Atlantic continues to offer a degree of underlying support.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market continued to slide as the week drew to a close, with sentiment remaining negative. Market sources described the trans-Atlantic market as predominantly mineral-focused, with little grain demand, while the limited fixtures being concluded were reported below previous levels as bids continued to edge lower. Fresh enquiry was also said to be limited and, although the tonnage count in the North Continent has reduced, a number of prompt ships remain in need of cover. Fronthaul activity from the US Gulf was said to have shown some improvement, although this has yet to translate into firmer rates, with the underlying fundamentals still described as largely imbalanced. EC South America saw a more encouraging end to the week. Despite an ample supply of ballasters arriving from the Indian Ocean, an improvement in demand helped lift sentiment, with firmer levels discussed and concluded fixture rates beginning to improve. Market sources described sentiment in the Pacific as edging towards the negative side, with activity slowing across both EC Australia and the North Pacific. Despite the quieter conditions, fundamentals were said to appear more balanced, with many market participants said to be taking a step back to assess their respective positions ahead of the new week. Conditions in Indonesia were less encouraging, particularly for older vessels, where limited employment opportunities continued to leave owners exposed to lower bids. The P5TC declined by $290 to close at $16,999.

Atlantic
The HC Glory (75,416 2012) open Tuna Tekra 20 October was said to have fixed a fronthaul trip via Santos at $18,250 plus $825,000 ballast bonus, although the charterer remains unknown. The Bettys Love (77,171 2008) open Kandla 26 October was placed on subjects for an EC South America fronthaul at around $15,250.

Asia
Pan Ocean was said to have placed on subjects the London 2012 (82,561 2007) Inchon prompt for a North Pacific round at $17,250, meanwhile the Ever Grace (82,039 2015) Tianjin 3 November was said to have fixed a Pacific round trip at $20,000.
SUPRAMAX
With the weekend approaching the 11TC average was down $72 to finish the week at $23,569, which is down $280 from last Friday. Most routes posted small declines, so the market doesn’t seem convinced enough to show any major weakness and awaits clearer direction, with some recent lower trades said to have reasons behind them. The Gooby (57,949 2012) was said to have fixed delivery passing Singapore prompt for a trip via Thailand to Australia with clinker at $20,000, whilst a Dolphin 64,000-dwt built 2025 open China was reportedly fixed for 12 months at $21,500 to an undisclosed Charterer. The Montrachtet (63,500 2026) fixed forward basis delivery ex yard Shanghai late November for 14 to 17 months at $21,000, again no Charterer was mentioned, and the ASP Frontier (57,298 2010) Fangcheng 7-13 November fixed 4 to 6 months at around $21,300 with PWSL. Platina took the Zaraar Hanif (55,693 2009) open Gangavaram 2-4 November for 2 to 3 laden legs minimum 60 days (first leg EC India to Oman), but the rate remained private.
HANDYSIZE
In keeping with the rest of the week, it was a slow finish with the HS7TC average down slightly to $18,255, which was just $106 down from last weeks close. The Atlantic routes were all negative, whilst the Pacific routes were all positive, although all moves were fairly small with the weekend approaching. The US Gulf continued to slide without an injection of new business and East coast South America was also down today, however there were mixed messages and varying opinions, with some saying the market was still very tight and rates to the Mediterranean were up. A 33,000-dwt was rumoured fixed delivery Pecem for a trip to the US Gulf at $25,000, a 36,000-dwt open Constanza was understood to have fixed a trip Baltic at $12,500 and the Marit Selmer (37,452 2013) open Iskenderun 6-9 November fixed a clean cargo to the US at a rumoured equivalent of $14,250, but no further details emerged. Despite rate levels being maintained in Asia, rumoured trades and fixtures were scarce, but the North Pacific was still the main driving force.

Market Fundamentals
Vale Q3 Results
In its 3Q26 production report, Vale reported iron ore output down 6.0 Mt year-on-year to 88.4 Mt, mainly reflecting a 7.7 Mt drop at Serra Norte. The decline was driven by lower run-of-mine availability, primarily due to operational constraints in mining areas near cave exclusion zones and at pit bottoms, as well as a one-off impact from lower fleet reliability. This was partly offset by a record 23.8 Mt quarter at S11D and the continued ramp-up of Capanema and VGR1. NOPAC OPENED THE WEEK WITH WHAT INITIALLY APPEARED TO BE A STABLE CARGO LIST AGAINST TONNAGE OPENING TOWARDS THE END OF THE MONTH, WITH BUSINESS CONCLUDED AROUND 20K BKI CJK. HOWEVER, AS SPOT TONNAGE CONTINUED TO BUILD, IT QUICKLY BECAME APPARENT THAT THESE LEVELS WOULD BE DIFFICULT TO REPRODUCE. BIDS SLIPPED TO THE $18K BKI CJK RANGE BY MIDWEEK. BY THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK, BIDS WERE INCREASINGLY HARD TO COME BY AND FIXTURES CONCLUDED AROUND USD 18.5K-19K BKI-CJK FOR TONNAGE ON THE MORE PROMPT SIDE. EAUS OPENED THE WEEK ON FIRMER FOOTING COMPARED TO NOPAC, CONTINUING TO COMMAND A PREMIUM OVER LONGER GRAIN ROUNDS. EARLY-WEEK LEVELS STOOD AT $19K BID VS $21K BKI CJK OFFERED FOR

SEASON AND A DWINDLING ATLANTIC MARKET. EAUS/INDIA WAS CLIPPED AROUND $21K BKI CJK MIDWEEK, ALTHOUGH CARGO FLOW REMAINED LIMITED, MAKING THIS A MORE OPPORTUNISTIC BUY. THIS WAS MAINLY OFF THE BACK OF SPOT CARGO FREIGHT IMPROVING ON THE BACK OF FIRMER BUNKERS, CHARTERERS WERE ABLE TO STRETCH SLIGHTLY HIGHER. AUSSIE GRAIN DEMAND ALSO CONTINUED TO PROVIDE A STEADY FLOW OF ENQUIRY, ALTHOUGH THE ABUNDANCE OF GRAIN CLEAN SHIPS MEANT THERE WAS LITTLE PREMIUM OVER STANDARD ROUNDS. INDO REMAINED DIFFICULT TO GAUGE, WITH OPERATORS FINDING THE ARBITRAGE INCREASINGLY CHALLENGING. INDO/SCHINA DEMAND WAS LIMITED AND THERE WAS A SEVERE LACK OF BALLAST INCENTIVE. FUNDAMENTALS OFFERED LITTLE ENCOURAGEMENT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK, WITH OWNERS LOWERING OFFERS INTO THE MID-HIGH TEENS BY WEDNESDAY/THURSDAY. OCCASIONAL PREMIUMS WERE PAID FOR INDO/PHILIPPINES WHEN CHARTERERS WERE TIGHT ON DATES AND UNDER PRESSURE TO COVER. A LARGE PROPORTION OF DEMAND REMAINED REDELIVERY INDIA-BOUND, YET OWNERS SHOWED LIMITED APPETITE TO REPOSITION, LEAVING RELATIVELY FEW EXCHANGE OPPORTUNITIES IN THE MARKET. OVERALL, SENTIMENT REMAINS FIRMLY NEGATIVE HEADING INTO THE COMING WEEK. TONNAGE IS YET TO CLEAR OUT AND WITH LITTLE SUPPORT COMING FROM THE ATLANTIC, THERE IS LIMITED INDICATION OF ANY MEANINGFUL RECOVERY IN THE NEAR TERM. Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977

segment, the “LEON W ISDOM ” (50k dwt 2008 HM D, Epoxy) has been sold at USD 26.9 mill basis delivery ex-yard upon passing her DD in November. Meanwhile, the same-aged “M AYFAIR” (50k dwt 2008 HM D, Epoxy) changed hands at USD 27 mill basis DD due and delivery in November. Elsewhere, the “ROSE M AKIS” (46k dwt 2005 Shin Kurushima, Epoxy) fetched USD 19 mill. Rounding off the week’s Tanker activity, the very modern Chemical Tanker “LONG DA 07” (14k dwt 2026 Zhoushan Ningshing, StSt) has been sold at USD 28.5 mill to Chinese buyers. Newbuilding Greek owner Pavimar are understood to have ordered 4 × 82,000dwt Kamsarmax Bulk Carriers at Hengli Heavy Industries, with deliveries scheduled during 2029. Pricing is estimated to be in the region of USD 37–38 mill per vessel. Meadway Bulkers have placed an order for 6 × 64,500dwt Ultramax Bulk Carriers at Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding in China, with deliveries scheduled during 2029–2030. Pricing is estimated at approximately USD 36 mill per vessel. Bahri and International Maritime Industries (IMI) have signed contracts for 3 × 320,000dwt VLCCs at a price of approximately USD 150 mill per vessel. The vessels will be constructed at IMI's facilities in Saudi Arabia, with deliveries scheduled between 2029 and 2030. Greek owner Venergy Maritime have placed an order for 2 + 2 × 306,000dwt VLCCs at Hengli Heavy Industries, with deliveries scheduled during the first half of 2029. Contract pricing has not been disclosed. Monaco-based Transocean Maritime Agencies have ordered 2 × 50,000dwt Medium Range Tankers at Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI), with deliveries expected during the second half of 2029. Pricing is estimated to be in the mid-USD 40 mill range per vessel. Central Mare are understood to have placed a repeat order for 2 × 50,000dwt Medium Range Tankers at K Shipbuilding, with deliveries scheduled during the first half of 2029. Pricing is estimated at approximately USD 53 mill per vessel, following the owner's previous order for two sister vessels at the same yard last summer, scheduled for delivery during 2028. Danaos Corporation have reportedly ordered 2 × 9,200TEU Container Vessels at Hudong- Zhonghua Shipbuilding, with deliveries expected during 2029. Pricing is understood to be approximately USD 109 mill per vessel. Namsung Shipping are understood to be in discussions with Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Corporation (DSIC) for an order of 2 + 2 × 7,100TEU Container Vessels, with deliveries proposed during 2030–2031. Pricing is estimated at approximately USD 89 mill per vessel. Peter Döhle Schiffahrts are understood to have ordered 4 × 3,700TEU Container Vessels at Chengxi Shipyard, with deliveries scheduled during 2029. Pricing is estimated to be in the region of USD 50 mill per vessel, while further commercial details have not been disclosed. KMTC (Korea Marine Transport Co.) have placed an order for 6 × 3,100TEU Container Vessels at Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. While pricing and delivery schedules have not been disclosed, values are estimated to be in the mid-to-high USD 40 mill range per vessel, with deliveries expected during the second half of 2029. Wallenius Wilhelmsen have signed contracts for 4 + 8 × 9,900CEU LNG dual-fuelled Pure Car and Truck Carriers (PCTCs) at China Merchants Jinling Shipyard (CMJL). The four firm vessels are scheduled for delivery from mid-2030 onward, with pricing estimated at approximately USD 120–125 mill per vessel.
